what_it_supplies: Printed p.106 footnote 26 gives the government purchase of the northwest Michigan/Madison property as June 21, 1839, price$262; it explicitly dates the PURCHASE, not the relocation.

The p.106 narrative about St Palais coming in December 1839 already describes O'Meara as having moved the old church from Lake Street to north Madison some yards west of Michigan. Together these statements support a retrospective later 1839 relocation window, with neither a move day nor a belfry completion date.
Printed p.107 says the NEW brick church 100 x 55 ft opened on Christmas Day 1843; those dimensions belong to the new brick building, not the first wooden church.

Printed p.112 says the OLD wooden church on north Madison between Wabash and Michigan was used for College St Mary on June 3, 1844. The old frame church therefore survived beyond 1843; a brick replacement opening does not date its demolition.
